question: Why did iQIYI put out 21 AI-generated short dramas in a quarter when its total revenue fell 10%?

rungs.question: Why is iQIYI making short dramas with AI at all?
rungs.answer: Management calls it an all-in AI strategy: use AI to widen the supply of shows and cut what each one costs to make. It says AI is already the main supply for micro dramas and is being pushed into longer formats, short-form dramas included.

evidence.quote: using artificial intelligence to expand content supply and reduce production costs
leverage AI to improve efficiency and reduce costs across content production and beyond
For short-form dramas, we launched 21 AIGC titles in Q3, up from Q2, and we will accelerate the rollout of AIGC short-form dramas going forward.

counter.text: On the same call management said live-action micro dramas earned several times more views and revenue per title than AI ones (webull.com: "Live-action micro dramas, by contrast, compete on quality, and their per-title views and revenue were several times higher than those of AIGC titles"). The 50% to 80% cost cuts quoted were for AI animation and children's titles, not short dramas.

rungs.question: Why does cheaper content matter to iQIYI this quarter?
rungs.answer: Revenue shrank on most lines: membership fell 6% on a lighter content slate and content distribution fell 38%. Content costs fell faster, by 13%, and that let the company return to a small non-GAAP operating profit of RMB25.0 million while still losing money on a GAAP basis.

evidence.quote: costs as a component of cost of revenues were RMB3.52 billion (US$525.3 million), decreasing 13% year over year, reflecting continued content strategy optimization.
Membership services revenue was RMB3.97 billion (US$592.2 million), decreasing 6% year over year, primarily due to a lighter content slate compared to
returned to a non-GAAP operating profit in the third quarter of 2026 as content costs fell, even as total revenue declined from the preceding quarter.

counter.text: The filing credits the content cost fall to "continued content strategy optimization" and the call summary to a shift toward revenue-sharing; neither says how much of it came from AI. GAAP operating loss was still RMB41.9 million.

rungs.question: Why do short dramas cut iQIYI's costs rather than just add to them?
rungs.answer: Most are revenue-sharing titles: creators make them and are paid by how they perform, so iQIYI swaps fixed upfront spending for payouts tied to viewing. Creators then have a reason to keep budgets low, which is where cheap AI production fits.

evidence.quote: Our revenue sharing model shifts a portion of iQIYI's content costs, especially from the original content cost side, from the fixed investment side to performance-based payout, reducing the upfront capital requirements and improving cash flow.
He said revenue-sharing arrangements shift some spending from upfront investment to payments tied to performance.
content creators are incentivized to optimize content costs, to have stricter cost control and allocate budget towards more visible production value

counter.text: That AI is the creators' answer to this incentive is inferred; no source says so. The sources do not say whether the 21 AI short dramas are among the 58 revenue-sharing short dramas launched in the quarter. The webull transcript also says 190 short dramas in 2026 is "a substantial increase from more than 220 in 2025", a figure that contradicts itself, likely a translation slip.

rungs.question: Why would AI make later titles cheaper still?
rungs.answer: In The Ferry Man series the lead actors licensed their likenesses and voices, and characters, sets and props were built as reusable digital assets, so each sequel reuses them. Each chapter earned back its production cost in its first week of release.

evidence.quote: The three lead actors licensed their likenesses and provided their own voiceovers, with digital character assets, scenes, and props developed as standardized, reusable assets.
Digital assets, including characters and scenes, as well as production expertise, can be reused across subsequent titles.
Three chapters of The Ferry Man generated more than CNY 14 million in revenue-sharing income, and each recouped its production cost within its first week of release, Gong said.

counter.text: This evidence is from an AI internet feature film series made with a major IP, not from the short dramas; no source gives production costs for any of the 21 AI short dramas. The October release is iQIYI's own announcement, and the producer says script development and post-production stayed largely the same as traditional workflows.

rungs.question: Why did iQIYI's short dramas reach No. 1 domestic share this quarter?
rungs.answer: In the call, management gave three reasons: a focus on suspense, branded theatres such as Undercurrent, and richer revenue-sharing terms for creators. It also called the format policy-supported. AI was not named among the reasons. The share figure is iQIYI citing Enlightent data.

evidence.quote: A key driver of our rapid breakthrough in short-form dramas was our strategic focus on specific dramas, particularly suspense.
Secondly, we are building user mindshare through branded theater operations with promising initial results.
According to Enlightent data cited by Gong, iQIYI ranked first in quarterly market share for short-form drama for the first time.

counter.text: Only one source (the webull transcript) carries management's reasons; the others report the ranking without explaining it. The record titles named, The Sixth Group of Fatal Case (over RMB57 million) and In the Dead of Winter, are not described as AI-made. Nothing read separates the AI titles' part in the share from the live-action titles'.

landing.shows: The sources show the AI short dramas sit inside a cost story: revenue fell, content costs fell faster, and revenue-sharing moved spending from upfront bets to payouts tied to viewing, with AI pitched as the way to make more titles for less. They do not show the AI titles drove the No. 1 short-drama share; management credited suspense, branded theatres and creator terms, and said live-action titles earn several times more per title.
landing.open_question: If live-action titles still earn several times more each, what share of iQIYI's first No. 1 short-drama quarter came from the 21 AI-made ones?
